SEC-AUTH.summary: The MCP route is a REST route whose permission callback requires a logged-in user with the 'read' capability, so WordPress's normal REST authentication applies. The plugin's dashboard and generated config use application passwords. The plugin adds no auth of its own.

SEC-UNAUTH.summary: An unauthenticated request fails the 'read' capability check at the transport and is refused. Nothing in the code makes the endpoint public.

SEC-CAPS.value: Per tool and per object: list-content uses the post type's edit_posts cap and filters rows by edit_post. get-content and save-content check edit_post on the id, and publish_posts for publish/private. read-debug-log needs manage_options. get-site-info and batch only need 'read'. Batch re-checks each inner tool's permission.
SEC-CAPS.summary: Each ability has its own permission callback, and content tools check per-post capabilities. get-site-info (which lists tool names, PHP and WP versions) is open to any logged-in user, including subscribers. That's a minor information leak.

SEC-SECRETS.value: No plugin-issued secrets; uses WordPress core application passwords (hashed by core). The Freemius license key is handled by the Freemius SDK.
SEC-SECRETS.summary: The plugin stores no API keys or tokens of its own. Credentials are WordPress application passwords, which core hashes and never shows again.

SEC-DEFAULT.value: The MCP server is registered as soon as the plugin is active. There is no on/off setting. Requests must be authenticated.
SEC-DEFAULT.summary: MCP is on by default, with no admin toggle, but every request needs a logged-in user. Pro Power Mode is a separate option that defaults to off.

SAFE-READONLY.summary: The code has no setting that blocks write tools for every connection. save-content stays available to anyone with the capability.

SAFE-SCOPE.value: The only control is the developer filter `track_debug_mcp_abilities`. Capabilities scope what each user can do. There is no admin UI for per-tool control.
SAFE-SCOPE.summary: A site owner cannot switch tools on or off from wp-admin. A developer can use a PHP filter, and WordPress roles limit what each credential can do.

value.mechanism: Annotations only. Free tools are all marked destructive=false. Batch refuses non-readonly tools unless they are explicitly non-destructive.

SAFE-CONFIRM.summary: The plugin has no confirmation step or approval queue. Its annotations are the only safeguard, and Pro destructive tools are not in the free code. The free save-content can overwrite a post and set it to publish, and it is annotated non-destructive.

SAFE-DELETE.value: No delete tools in the free plugin.
SAFE-DELETE.summary: The free plugin has no delete tool. Deleting is only possible through Pro Power Mode (run-php and others), which is not in this code.

SAFE-LOG.value: Free tool calls are not logged. Only adapter errors go to debug.log through ErrorLogMcpErrorHandler, and registration failures go to error_log. The read-debug-log audit level reads that log.
SAFE-LOG.summary: There is no admin-viewable record of who called which tool. The plugin only writes errors to debug.log, and admins can read them through the read-debug-log tool.

CAP-TOOLS.summary: The free server exposes 6 tools. Pro adds more through the `track_debug_mcp_abilities` filter: Elementor, WooCommerce, Yoast, Rank Math, Site Kit, cache purge, run-php, get-option, list-plugins and others. The Pro code is not in this plugin.

CAP-AREAS.summary: The free plugin covers posts and pages only. Pro lists media, plugins, themes, users, settings and WooCommerce.

T2.tool: save-content (HTML or block markup, run through wp_kses_post; no image upload in free)

T3.tool: get-content + save-content (content replaces the whole field, so the client must send the full text; no append mode)

T8.tool: save-content: publish needs publish_posts; contributors and subscribers cannot publish. Subscribers fail edit_posts.

CAP-TASKS.summary: The free plugin handles listing and drafting. Media upload, plugin list, settings and delete are Pro-only.

STD-ABILITIES.value: Registers 6 abilities with wp_register_ability under the track-debug category and exposes them through a scoped copy of wordpress/mcp-adapter.
STD-ABILITIES.summary: It uses the Abilities API and ships its own namespaced copy of the MCP Adapter.

STD-TRANSPORT.summary: MCP runs in WordPress at /wp-json/track-debug/mcp through the adapter's HttpTransport, which targets the 2025-11-25 spec.

STD-FREE.summary: The MCP connection and basic post/page tools are free. Everything beyond posts and pages needs the paid add-on (Pro with a Freemius license).

HOST-LOCAL.value: Generated config uses @automattic/mcp-wordpress-remote with WP_API_URL and an application password. WordPress allows application passwords over HTTP on local environments.
HOST-LOCAL.summary: Claude Desktop can connect to a local site with an application password and the bridge. The readme says local development follows WordPress configuration.

HOST-PUBLIC.value: Relies on core application passwords and REST. No handling of a stripped Authorization header, CORS, or WAF/caching notes was found in the PHP.
HOST-PUBLIC.summary: It works on hosts that pass the Authorization header and allow application passwords. The plugin has no fallback for stripped headers or other common host problems.

steps: Pick the client and copy the config
Paste it into the Claude Desktop JSON config (needs Node/npx)
Restart the client and ask for site info

SETUP-STEPS.summary: The readme lists 7 steps. It takes about 6 once the dashboard walks you through the password and config.

SETUP-NOTERM.value: Requires pasting JSON or TOML into the client config and having Node/npx installed. No OAuth or connector-URL flow was found.
SETUP-NOTERM.summary: A site owner has to edit a client config file and have npx on their computer. The plugin offers no connector URL for Claude's custom connector.

SETUP-GUIDE.value: The dashboard has a Connection tab that generates client-specific config and prompts with the site's own endpoint, and an Overview tab that shows the endpoint URL.
SETUP-GUIDE.summary: The admin screen provides copyable, site-specific configs for Claude Desktop, Cursor and Codex, and shows the endpoint URL.

value: Freemius checkout URLs in the dashboard
DOCS.summary: Setup is documented in the readme and in the dashboard. No docs site link was found in the PHP, and the dashboard links mostly point to purchase pages.

notes: I did not read the built admin JavaScript in full (build/index.js is minified), so the dashboard claims rest on the readme and the strings I found. The server instructions field tells the model about Pro tools (run-php, get-option, elementor-*, wc-*), but those abilities are not in the free code, so the free tool list is only the 6 shown. The plugin's tool-call "audit log" mentioned in the read-debug-log description is written by the Pro add-on, not the free plugin. The batch runner would allow any registered ability whose annotations say it does not change data, or that is marked non-destructive, so a Pro or third-party ability with a loose annotation could run inside batch. The 'destructive' annotation on save-content is false even though it can overwrite post content and publish. get-site-info is callable by any logged-in user with the 'read' capability, such as a subscriber. The HttpTransport default permission is only 'read', so every authenticated user can connect to the MCP endpoint.
